topic: Motion of the Centre of Mass
title: Rocket Bursts! Motion of the Centre of Mass | Class 11 Physics
description:
A diver flips off a board, a thrown hammer spins in the air, a festival rocket bursts into pieces. Messy motion, yet in each one a single point moves in a smooth, simple curve. When Aarav watches a rocket burst at the top of its flight, the pieces fly apart, but one point keeps the old curve as if nothing happened. Which point, and why? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn how the centre of mass moves.

We weight velocities by mass to get the velocity of the centre of mass, and meet the big result: total mass times the acceleration of the centre of mass equals the total external force. On a live motion notebook a rocket flies on a parabola and bursts at the top into two equal halves: one falls straight down, the other shoots forward, and the centre of mass keeps the very same curve, landing at 40 m while the halves land at 20 m and 60 m. A slow-mo replay freezes the burst to show the equal and opposite internal forces and the unchanged weight Mg. We prove M A = F ext step by step, see link by link why the burst does not matter, compare a rocket with and without a burst side by side, test the idea with a person walking on a boat, and solve two blocks on ice with a spring between them. Then the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question on a shell that splits into unequal pieces, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
